editorial:
You follow a burger-loving hit man, his thoughtful partner, a gangster's wife, and a washed-up boxer through a wild crime story that jumps around in time. The mood is cool, funny, and tense, with sharp conversations, sudden violence, and strange little moments that make the whole thing feel alive. You never quite know what will happen next, and that surprise is part of the fun. Every scene has its own weird energy.

The acting is strong, the dialogue is memorable, and the pacing keeps you locked in even when scenes slow down. It can be bloody, talky, and a little long, so it is not for everyone. If you enjoy dark comedy, crime stories, and bold storytelling, this is a great pick. The soundtrack also gives it extra style.
endingExplained: In the final diner scene, two robbers try to take Jules and Vincent's mysterious briefcase, but Jules turns the tables and delivers his famous speech. Instead of killing them, he lets them leave with the money, choosing mercy and a new path. He and Vincent walk out together, but because the story jumps around, you have already seen Vincent's violent end elsewhere. The glowing briefcase is never explained, leaving one last fun mystery.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark comedy, crime stories, and bold nonlinear storytelling.
